text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to understand. When developers refactor, they might rename variables, break large functions into smaller ones, or remove duplicate code. These changes improve readability, which means other programmers can read and work with the code more easily. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is written quickly without proper design. Although refactoring takes time, it saves effort in the long run and makes future changes safer and faster.
